subject.title: [Slack] Agent lacks visibility into own channel messages from DM sessions

question: What Slack self-activity recall boundary should OpenClaw support when a DM/main session asks about the agent's own outbound channel sends?
rationale: The source-level gap is clear, but the fix chooses who may learn about channel activity from a DM, how long outbound activity is retained, and which canonical store owns that data.

options.title: Narrow self-activity ledger
options.body: Record agent-authored outbound Slack deliveries in a canonical store and expose only authorized self-activity summaries to DM/main sessions.

options.title: Shared session grouping
options.body: Treat this as part of broader configurable shared Slack/Discord channel sessions, accepting larger context, migration, and privacy design work.

options.title: Keep isolation documented
options.body: Keep current session isolation and document that operators must opt into broader session visibility or manual memory workflows.

recommendation.title: Narrow self-activity ledger
recommendation.body: Record agent-authored outbound Slack deliveries in a canonical store and expose only authorized self-activity summaries to DM/main sessions.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the strongest visible combination of prior review context and recent Slack/session routing history for this boundary decision.
